I have what I need. Let me assess Section 6.1 against the rule.

**Analysis:**

The only restriction binding us is § 6.1 (p0037). Testing it against the fallback:

| Fallback element | § 6.1 |
|---|---|
| Named competing product | ✓ Scope tied to defined "Deerskin Products" and named competitors (Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled) — not "any competing business" |
| During the term only | ✓ No post-term tail on the Company |
| Capped at 12 months | ✓ Term is one (1) year, auto-renewing annually, terminable on 90 days' notice (§ 4.1) |
| Carve-outs | ✓ § 6.2 (closeout website), plus "Deerskin Products" excludes closeout merchandise and Joan Cook Catalog products; § 8(b) grandfathers the Globix Agreement |

Also relevant on direction: § 6.3 imposes a *two-year post-term* restriction on **HDI** — that binds the counterparty and benefits us, so it is not flagged. The restriction is also narrow in field-of-use: it only bars "any project similar to the Site on the Internet," leaving our catalog, retail and sourcing businesses untouched.

No walk-away trigger: there is no post-term non-compete on the Company and the scope is defined rather than open-ended.

input.quote: Except as provided in Section 6.2, during the term of this Agreement, the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products (including, without limitation, the products of Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled)
input.rationale:
The document does contain one exclusivity covenant binding us (§ 6.1, p0037), so the rule is not "missing," but it sits at the playbook fallback and is therefore compliant and not redlined.

Fallback elements are all met on the material terms: (1) scope is limited to a defined product set ("Deerskin Products," defined at p0005) plus named competitors (Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled) rather than an undefined "any competing business"; (2) it applies "during the term of this Agreement" only, with no post-term tail on the Company; (3) duration is effectively capped within 12 months because § 4.1 (p0024) sets a one (1) year term that renews only in one-year increments and is terminable by either Party on 90 days' notice, so we can exit the restriction at will; and (4) meaningful carve-outs exist — § 6.2 (p0040/p0041) preserves our right to run our own closeout-merchandise website, and the "Deerskin Products" definition expressly excludes closeout merchandise and our Joan Cook Catalog products, with § 8(b) additionally grandfathering the Globix Agreement.

The field of use is narrow: it only bars participation in "any project similar to the Site on the Internet," leaving our catalog, retail store and sourcing/procurement businesses entirely unrestricted, so there is no restriction on what products we may buy or build offline.

No walk-away trigger applies: there is no post-term non-compete on the Company and the scope is not open-ended.

Two sub-elements fall short of the preferred position but are noted here rather than flagged: the phrase "companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled" is somewhat elastic, and there is no express carve-out for internal development or acquisitions (e.g., a business acquired that happens to run a similar site). If this agreement is reopened for other reasons, we would add an acquisitions/internal-development carve-out and tighten "companies similar to" to an agreed list.

On direction: § 6.3 (p0042) imposes a heavier two-year post-term restriction on HDI. That binds the counterparty and benefits us, so it is expressly not flagged under this rule.
